cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at activity selection problem which can be solved using grid algorithm.
So here the problem statement says that given the n number of activities with their start and end times,
we need to select the maximum number of activities that can be performed by a single person.
Assuming that a person can only work on a single activity at a time.
So initially this problem statement might not be clear.
Now let's look at this with the real life example.
So let's say we have an activity list over here.
Activity one activity two.
And it continues until activity six.
Now here we have the start time and end time.
So we need to find the number of the activities from these activities that a person can perform.
So here take into account that a person cannot perform the two activities at the same time.
So let's say if a person starts performing the activity one.
So activity one starts at 8:00 and ends at 2:00.
While doing this it cannot perform the second activity.
You see that this is starting at 11:00 and finishes at 12:00 and he cannot do activity three also and
activity four also.
Activity five also and he can do only activity six.
So this means that if we select the activity one he can do only activity one and activity six.
Now he can perform only two activities.
Now the question is can we improve this solution to perform more activities here.
So let's see how it works.
So if we look at this problem very closely, we can see that a person cannot perform another activity
until he will be free.
So he becomes free only after the finish time of current activity.
Basically, the important thing over here is finish time.
One approach is we can sort activities based on the finish time and then we can perform the activities.
So if we sort these activities based on the finish time, our table will look like this.
So as you can see the place of the activities changes.
Now if the person performs in this order, we can easily see that he can perform four activities in
this case.
So as you can see, we have improved the our solution from two activities to four.
Activities.
So by sorting the activities based on finish time, we have improved our solution.
Now let's see why we call this algorithm a grid algorithm.
Now the key word over here is the freeze, which means at a given point in time, we take the best solution
and freeze it so we never come back to it.
So here we did the same thing.
We take A3 as the best solution at this time.
Then after A3 we take A2, which is the best solution in this case.
Then because A2 finishes at 12, we cannot take A1.
Because A2 finishes at 12:00, we cannot take the A1.
Then we took the A5 which starts at 1:00.
So this was the best solution at that time.
And it continues like this.
So this is why it's called the grid algorithm, because we find the local optimum solution which leads
to the global solution for activity selection problem.
Now let's look at the code of this problem.
So here I'll bring the code.
Then we will have the activities on the right.
So let's debug this code to see how this is working.
So the first thing that we are doing we are sorting these activities based on the finish time.
So to be able to do that, we are going to take the second element in the inner array.
That's why we have used over here index of one.
So after sorting it it's going to become like this.
Then we are going to create an empty array which is going to be selected activities.
Then initially last end time is going to be zero because we are using the end time to compare with the
next activity start time.
So that's why we need this variable over here.
Then we are going to start to loop through the these activities.
So in this case for the first activity the start time is nine and the end time is ten.
So first we are going to check that if the start time is greater than the last end time.
So last end time initially is zero.
So that's why we see that nine is greater than zero.
This means that we are going to select this activity as a selected activity.
Then we will take this activities end time.
Put it in the last end time.
So the end time is ten.
So last end time is going to be ten.
Then we are going to continue to the next activity.
Now the next activity is from 11 to 12.
So here again, the last end time is ten and the start time is 11, which is greater than ten.
So we are going to select this activity and put it in the selected activities.
And we are going to update the last end time with this end time.
So in this case the end time is 12.
Then I'm going to put the selected activities like this to have the more space then we are going to
continue next activity.
Now the next activity starts at 8:00 and ends at two.
Now the last end time is 12 which is greater than the start time.
So that's why we are not going to take this activity.
Then we are going to continue to the next activity.
Now the next activity starts at 1:00 pm which is greater than 12.
So that's why we are going to take this activity and put it in the selected activities.
And we are going to update the last end time with the end time, which is 15.
Then we will continue to the next activity.
Now the next activity starts at 1:00 which is less than the 3:00.
So that's why we are not going to take this.
Then the last activity starts at 4:00 which is greater than 3:00.
So that's why we are going to take this activity as well.
And we are going to update the last end time.
So this was the last activity in the activities array.
That's why at the end it's just going to return the the selected activities array.
So as you can see we have successfully selected four activities.
